title: Instant payments and AI fraud: the detection window problem
linkedinPost:
The EBA found that fraud risk on instant payments is 10 times higher than on regular credit transfers.

Most bank fraud defenses weren't built for it.

APP scams — where a fraudster convinces a legitimate customer to authorise a payment to an attacker account — are the primary vector on instant rails. The bank sees an authorised transaction. The fraud happened in the WhatsApp message 20 minutes earlier.

Generative AI has compounded this:

• Deepfake video impersonating CFOs. The $25M Arup transfer wasn't a system hack — it was an authorised payment. (BBC, January 2025.)
• Synthetic identities aged over months from leaked KYC data before being activated as mule accounts.
• Adaptive probing of fraud models to calibrate attack patterns below detection thresholds.

Here is what I would actually build:

• VoP — but audit implementation quality before a supervisor does. Name matching accuracy varies enormously across PSPs.
• Behavioural biometrics at payment initiation. Preliminary research shows 90% effectiveness in identifying mule activity (TrustSphere, 2026). The hardest control to evade.
• EU AI Act Article 12 logging wired into every fraud model from day one — as a Supabase event log that satisfies DORA incident reporting simultaneously.
• Post-settlement graph analytics in the seconds after settlement. The mule network is visible if you have the infrastructure to look.

JPMorgan cut false positives 20% with ML scoring. That is analyst time recovered and customer friction removed.

Revenue per employee in payments ops rises when fraud detection is accurate, not just sensitive.

Full piece + the Fraud Defense Clock I use to structure this — link in comments.

mainEntity.name: What is APP fraud in instant payments?

acceptedAnswer.text: APP (authorised push payment) fraud occurs when a fraudster persuades a legitimate account holder to send an instant payment to an attacker-controlled account. The payment is authorised by the customer, meaning technical fraud controls at the transaction layer do not trigger. APP fraud is the dominant fraud type on instant payment rails in Europe and is not addressed by Verification of Payee alone.

mainEntity.name: How does Verification of Payee reduce instant payments fraud?

acceptedAnswer.text: Verification of Payee checks that the beneficiary name matches the IBAN before executing an instant payment. Under EU Regulation 2024/886, it became mandatory for euro area PSPs in October 2025. VoP directly reduces account-takeover and misdirected payment fraud. It does not prevent APP fraud where the attacker has provided a correctly named account — the account name matches, but the account belongs to the fraudster.

mainEntity.name: Does the EU AI Act apply to fraud detection AI systems in banks?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Fraud detection AI at regulated financial institutions is classified as high-risk under EU AI Act Annex III. Article 12 automated audit logging, Article 14 human oversight controls, and Article 13 transparency documentation are all required. The August 2026 application deadline for high-risk systems applies to fraud detection models and is not subject to the Digital Omnibus deferral that applies to some other Annex III categories.

mainEntity.name: How does AI fraud detection reduce false positives in banking?

acceptedAnswer.text: AI fraud models trained on behavioural, network, and contextual signals distinguish legitimate from fraudulent transactions with higher precision than rule-based systems. JPMorgan Chase reported a 20% reduction in false positive rates after deploying ML-based scoring. Reduced false positives lower dispute handling cost, reduce customer friction on legitimate instant payments, and free fraud analyst capacity for genuine investigation rather than alert review.
